terms.definition: The number of protons in an element's atoms; the number that identifies the element.
terms.function: Names the element, places it on the periodic table, and (in a neutral atom) equals the electron count.
terms.whereItIs: Printed at the top of each element's card on the periodic table.
terms.whyItMatters: It is the single number that defines what an element is.

terms.definition: The positively charged particle in the nucleus that the atomic number counts.
terms.function: Gives the nucleus its charge and its identity — the proton count IS the atomic number.
terms.whereItIs: Inside the nucleus cluster beside the card, shown as the coral spheres.
terms.whyItMatters: Every atomic number is literally a count of protons.

terms.definition: A pure substance made of atoms that all share the same atomic number.
terms.function: Gives matter its identity — each element owns its unique atomic number.
terms.whereItIs: Each box on the periodic table is one element.
terms.whyItMatters: The atomic number is how elements are told apart.

terms.definition: A chart that lists all known elements, ordered by increasing atomic number.
terms.function: Organizes elements so that similar ones line up together in columns and rows.
terms.whereItIs: The slab of tiles shown below the card in the model.
terms.whyItMatters: It is the master map of chemistry, built on the atomic number.
